newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end up on corn rally, Brazil weather.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end up on corn rally, Brazil weather.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures closed higher on Monday, in line with late gains in corn, as bullish South American weather outweighed poor USDA export data, traders said.
"They didn't get all that much rain in Brazil but there is some in the forecast," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter.
Weekend rains missed key growing regions in Brazil's Rio Grande do Sul but forecasts called for another shot of moisture this week.
The bullish weather forecast, coupled with strength in corn, supplanted bearish input from USDA's export inspections.
USDA on Monday pegged export inspections at 16.7 million bushels, well below last week's 35.3 million bushels.
Soybeans had traded lower most of the session in response to those figures but pit sources said selling evaporated late as corn rallied.
Sell stops were hit above $7.50 per bushel in the March, stifling the late rally attempt. Technical traders pegged support Tuesday in the March at $7.44-3/4 per bushel and resistance at $7.52-3/4.
Soybeans closed 3-3/4 to 1-1/2 cents per bushel higher with March up 2-1/4 at $7.49-3/4.
On the day, Cargill Investor Services bought six million bushels May and Refco Inc bought 2.5 million March and 1.5 million May, traders said.
FCC reportedly bought one million bushels each March, May and July while Dean Witter bought 1.5 million March.
In options, FCC sold 650 $8.00 March calls at 4-1/2 cents per bushel, traders said.
Volume was estimated by CBOT at 37,500 contracts, against Friday's actual volume of 34,038 contracts, according to CBOT figures.
